rules.description: Statutory paid annual leave: 4 weeks (reg. 13) + 1.6 weeks additional (reg. 13A) = 5.6 weeks, capped at 28 days.

source.title: Working Time Regulations 1998, reg. 13A (entitlement to additional annual leave)

versions.notes: Reg. 13(1): four weeks; reg. 13A(2)(e): 1.6 weeks in any leave year beginning on or after 1 April 2009; reg. 13A(3): aggregate maximum 28 days. Applies per LEAVE YEAR beginning on/after effectiveFrom. GOV.UK (https://www.gov.uk/holiday-entitlement-rights) confirms 5.6 weeks, 28-day cap and that employers may include bank holidays. Reg. 13(9)(b): no payment in lieu except on termination. Irregular-hours accrual: see leave.irregular_hours_accrual. rules.description: Irregular-hours and part-year workers accrue leave at 12.07% of hours worked (reg. 15B) and may be paid rolled-up holiday pay (reg. 16A).

source.title: Working Time Regulations 1998, reg. 15B (irregular hours and part-year workers)

versions.notes: Reg. 15B(1): applies to irregular hours workers and part-year workers in respect of leave years beginning on or after 1 April 2024; 15B(3): accrues at 12.07% of hours worked in the pay period; 15B(4): max 28 days per leave year. Reg. 16A (inserted 1.1.2024 by S.I. 2023/1426): holiday pay for reg. 15B leave may be paid as a 12.07% uplift; itemised pay statements must show the holiday pay amount (16A(7)). Source for 16A: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1998/1833/regulation/16A. For leave years beginning on or before 31 March 2024 GOV.UK says accrual is not required (not modelled). Extent: England, Wales and Scotland only (legislation.gov.uk marks the provision "E+W+S"); Northern Ireland has separate legislation, so this version does not answer GB-NIR. Phase 5 (verified 2026-10-18): reg. 15B(3) leave accrues "on the last day of each pay period"; reg. 15B(5) a fraction of an hour is treated as zero if less than 30 minutes and as one hour if 30 minutes or more. GOV.UK worked example (68 hours in June -> 8.2076 -> 8 hours): https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/simplifying-holiday-entitlement-and-holiday-pay-calculations/holiday-pay-and-entitlement-reforms-from-1-january-2024 (updated 1 April 2024).

rules.description: Carry-over of untaken statutory leave (reg. 13 EU-derived 4 weeks vs reg. 13A additional 1.6 weeks).

rules.description: Gender pay gap reporting (England, Scotland and Wales).

value.fullPayRelevantEmployee: relevant employee not paid at a reduced rate or nil in the relevant pay period as a result of being on leave

source.title: GOV.UK — Gender pay gap reporting: when to report

versions.notes: GOV.UK guidance: 250+ employees on the snapshot date (headcount, not FTE); snapshot 31 March (most public authorities) / 5 April (private, voluntary, all other public authorities); deadlines 30 March / 4 April the following year. Applies to England, Scotland and Wales; different rules for public authorities in Scotland and Wales; NI-based employers with 250+ employees in GB are included (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/gender-pay-gap-reporting-guidance-for-employers/who-needs-to-report). Private-sector regs (S.I. 2017/172) in force 6 April 2017; reg. 2(2) publish within 12 months of snapshot. ERA 2025 equality action plans (GOV.UK guidance 7 April 2026) not modelled. Extent: England, Wales and Scotland only (legislation.gov.uk marks the provision "E+W+S"); Northern Ireland has separate legislation, so this version does not answer GB-NIR. Phase 5 (verified 2026-10-18): the six figures are S.I. 2017/172 reg. 2(1)(a)-(f) (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2017/172/regulation/2); definitions reg. 1 ("full-pay relevant employee", "snapshot date"), reg. 6 hourly rate (weekly multiplier 7 / days in the relevant pay period, a month = 30.44 days, a year = 365.25 days), regs. 8-11 gaps expressed as a percentage of the male figure, reg. 10(2)/12(3) bonus period = 12 months ending with the snapshot date, reg. 13 quartiles (equal sections so far as possible; employees on the same rate spanning bands split in the same male/female proportion). Remainder allocation (1 -> lower; 2 -> lower and upper middle; 3 -> lower, lower middle and upper middle), worked examples and "whole percentages or rounded to one decimal place" from GOV.UK "Making your calculations" (updated 21 May 2026, https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/gender-pay-gap-reporting-guidance-for-employers/making-your-calculations). The guidance gives no rule on which sex/gender classification to use: left to the employer (legal review).

coverage.notes: UK pack: bank holidays for England & Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland (2019 onwards, checked against gov.uk/bank-holidays.json) and core GB employment rules verified on legislation.gov.uk / gov.uk on 2026-10-18. Includes Employment Rights Act 2025 changes in force (SSP from 6 April 2026; day-one paternity leave from 6 April 2026) and commenced-but-future (unfair dismissal 6 months from 1 January 2027, S.I. 2026/559). Every rule version lists the UK nations it was verified for (`regions`, ADR-0022). Northern Ireland has separate employment legislation: lookups for GB-NIR are answered by the GB-NIR pack and by the UK-wide GB rules only (minimum wage, right to work); every other GB rule is not returned for GB-NIR (it fails explicitly). A bare `GB` lookup returns the Great Britain (England, Wales, Scotland) law. Pending legal review.
